items.stem: Which activity best represents governance rather than management in a COBIT-style model?

options.text: The board setting risk appetite and directing investment priorities
options.rationale: Correct: setting direction, risk appetite and monitoring outcomes are Evaluate-Direct-Monitor (governance) activities.

options.text: A team deploying a patch to production servers
options.rationale: Deploying patches is an operational management (build/run) activity.

options.text: An analyst writing a test plan for a release
options.rationale: Test planning sits within management domains, not governance.

options.text: A developer fixing a defect found in testing
options.rationale: Defect fixing is a management/operational task.

items.explanation: Correct: setting direction, risk appetite and monitoring outcomes are Evaluate-Direct-Monitor (governance) activities.

items.stem: In the goals cascade, what triggers the flow toward alignment goals and objectives?

options.rationale: Vendor roadmaps are external inputs, not the cascade trigger.
Correct: stakeholder drivers and enterprise goals initiate the cascade down to alignment goals and governance/management objectives.
Audit scheduling is downstream assurance, not the cascade origin.

options.text: Available IT budget for the year
options.rationale: Budget constrains delivery but does not originate the goals cascade.
